[[Gubernatorial elections]] are scheduled to be held in the [[United States]] on November 3, 2026. This election will take place in 36 states and three territories. The previous gubernatorial elections for this group of states took place in [[2022 United States gubernatorial elections|2022]], except in [[New Hampshire]] and [[Vermont]], where governors serve two-year terms and elected their governors in [[2024 United States gubernatorial elections|2024]]. 

Fifteen of the thirty-six states and two of the three United States territories with elections in this cycle have officially [[Term limits in the United States|term-limited]] incumbents.

== Partisan composition ==
{{unsourced section|date=October 2026}}
Going into the election, there are 26 [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governors and 24 [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governors in the United States. This class of governors is made up of 18 Republicans and 18 Democrats. Republicans are defending two governorships in states that [[Kamala Harris]] won in 2024 (New Hampshire and Vermont). Democrats are defending five governorships in states that [[Donald Trump]] won in 2024 (Arizona, Kansas, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin).

== Retirements ==
22 incumbent governors (11 Democrats, 10 Republican, and 1 Independent) are retiring. 17 incumbent governors (8 Democrats and 9 Republicans) are term-limited. 5 incumbent governors (3 Democrats, 1 Republican, and 1 Independent) have announced they are not seeking reelection.

==Incumbents defeated==
===In primary elections===
====Democrats====
One Democrat lost renomination. The last elected incumbent governor to lose renomination was [[Neil Abercrombie]] of [[Hawaii]] in [[2014 United States gubernatorial elections|2014]].{{efn|[[Jeff Colyer]], who succeeded [[Sam Brownback]] as [[List of governors of Kansas|Governor of Kansas]] in 2017 and finished out Brownback's term, ran for a full term in [[2018 Kansas gubernatorial election|2018]] but lost the primary to [[Kris Kobach]], who lost the general election to [[Laura Kelly]].<ref name=McKeeLoses/>}}

#[[2026 Rhode Island gubernatorial election|Rhode Island]]: [[Dan McKee]] lost renomination to [[Helena Buonanno Foulkes|Helena Foulkes]].<ref name=McKeeLoses>{{cite news |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/helena-foulkes-winner-rhode-island-democratic-governor-primary-mckee-rcna596559 |title=Rhode Island Gov. Dan McKee loses Democratic primary to businesswoman Helena Foulkes |publisher=NBC News |last=Edelman |first=Adam |date=September 9, 2026 |accessdate=September 9, 2026}}</ref>

== Predictions ==

Several sites and individuals published predictions of competitive seats. These predictions looked at factors such as the strength of the [[incumbent]] (if the incumbent was running for reelection) and the other candidates, and the state's partisan lean (reflected in part by the state's [[Cook Partisan Voting Index]] rating). The predictions assigned ratings to each seat, indicating the predicted advantage that a party had in winning that seat. Most election predictors used:
* "<u>tossup</u>": no advantage
* "<u>tilt</u>" (used by some predictors): advantage that is not quite as strong as "lean"
* "<u>lean</u>": slight advantage
* "<u>likely</u>": significant, but surmountable, advantage
* "<u>safe</u>" or "<u>solid</u>": near-certain chance of victory<!-- Colors and sorting:

In many cases, the incumbent has yet to say their intention of running for another term. If an incumbent intends to retire then place "<br />{{Small|(Retiring)}}" after the incumbent's name.

See [[Template:USRaceRating]] for how to apply rating.

{{Main|2026 Alabama gubernatorial election}}

{{See also|2026 Alabama lieutenant gubernatorial election}}
Governor [[Kay Ivey]], a Republican, was re-elected in [[2022 Alabama gubernatorial election|2022]] with 67.4% of the vote. She will be term-limited by the [[Constitution of Alabama]] in 2026 and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive full term. Republican [[US Senator|U.S. Senator]] [[Tommy Tuberville]] entered the gubernatorial race in May 2025, joined by former candidate for [[Alabama's 6th congressional district]] in [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Alabama#District 6|2024]] Ken McFeeters<ref name="AL2026R"/> and event center operations manager Will Santivasci.<ref name=ALcom>{{Cite web|url=https://www.al.com/politics/2026/02/alabama-2026-election-everyone-running-for-governor.html|title=Alabama 2026 election: Everyone running for governor|last=Gann|first=Heather|website=AL.com|date=February 5, 2026|access-date=February 8, 2026}}</ref>

Democratic candidates include former U.S. Senator [[Doug Jones (politician)|Doug Jones]]; the [[2022 Alabama gubernatorial election|2022]] gubernatorial nominee Yolanda Flowers; [[Will Boyd]], a former city councilor of [[Greenville, Illinois]], and the nominee for Alabama Lieutenant Governor in [[2018 Alabama lieutenant gubernatorial election|2018]] and for U.S. Senate in [[2022 United States Senate election in Alabama|2022]]; pastor Ja'Mel Brown; candidate for governor in 2022 Chad Chig Martin;<ref name="AL2026D"/> and former state representative [[Nathan Mathis]].<ref name=ALcom/>

As Jones and Tuberville won their respective primaries, the gubernatorial election will be a rematch of the [[2020 United States Senate election in Alabama|2020 United States Senate election]], which saw Tuberville defeat Jones. Tuberville has faced several [[2026 Alabama gubernatorial election#Challenges to Tuberville's eligibility|challenges to his eligibility for the governorship]].

{{Main|2026 Alaska gubernatorial election}}

Governor [[Mike Dunleavy (politician)|Mike Dunleavy]], a Republican, was re-elected in [[2022 Alaska gubernatorial election|2022]] with 50.3% of the vote. He will be term-limited by the [[Constitution of Alaska]] in 2026 and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term. 

A [[nonpartisan primary]] was held on August 18, 2026, with the top four candidates advancing to the general election, which will be conducted using [[Ranked-choice voting in the United States|ranked-choice voting]]. The advancing candidates are Republicans former state Attorney General [[Treg Taylor]],<ref name="TaylorAK">{{cite news |first1=Josiah |last1=Pike |work=[[Alaska's News Source]] |access-date=September 17, 2025 |url=https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2025/09/17/former-attorney-general-treg-taylor-announces-gubernatorial-campaign/ |date=September 17, 2025 |title=Former Attorney General Treg Taylor announces gubernatorial campaign}}</ref> businesswoman Bernadette Wilson;<ref name="AKGOP">{{cite news |last1=Brooks |first1=James |title=Third Republican candidate, Bernadette Wilson, enters Alaska governor's race |url=https://alaskabeacon.com/2025/05/14/third-republican-candidate-bernadette-wilson-enters-alaska-governors-race/ |access-date=May 14, 2025 |work=Alaska Beacon |date=May 14, 2025}}</ref> former [[Anchorage, Alaska|Anchorage]] mayor [[Dave Bronson]];<ref name="BronsonAK">{{cite web |last1=Barnwell |first1=Jack |publisher=[[Fairbanks Daily News-Miner]] |access-date=October 2, 2025 |url=https://www.newsminer.com/news/alaska_news/dave-bronson-former-anchorage-mayor-enters-governors-race/article_5585e6aa-07f1-433b-b298-03c0b86758af.html |date=October 2, 2025 |title=Dave Bronson, former Anchorage mayor, enters governor's race}}</ref> and Democrat former state representative [[Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins]].<ref name="Claman">{{cite news |last1=Rosen |first1=Yereth |title=Anchorage state senator enters crowded Alaska gubernatorial field |url=https://alaskabeacon.com/briefs/anchorage-state-senator-enters-crowded-alaska-gubernatorial-field/ |access-date=November 10, 2025 |work=Alaska Beacon |date=November 10, 2025}}</ref>

After initially finishing second in the primary, former state senator [[Tom Begich]] withdrew and endorsed Kreiss-Tomkins, allowing fifth-place finisher Taylor to advance to the general election.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Samuels |first1=Iris |title=Tom Begich says he will withdraw from Alaska governor's race |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/08/28/tom-begich-says-he-will-withdraw-from-alaska-governors-race/ |access-date=August 29, 2026 |work=[[Anchorage Daily News]] |date=August 28, 2026}}</ref> However, the Alaska Public Offices Commission recommended against certifying Taylor's candidacy after finding that his financial disclosure did not substantially comply with state law.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Samuels |first1=Iris |title=Alaska campaign watchdog says Treg Taylor should not be allowed to run for governor |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/08/28/alaska-campaign-watchdog-says-treg-taylor-should-not-be-allowed-to-run-for-governor/ |access-date=August 29, 2026 |work=[[Anchorage Daily News]] |date=August 28, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260829081050/https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/08/28/alaska-campaign-watchdog-says-treg-taylor-should-not-be-allowed-to-run-for-governor/ |archive-date=August 29, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> On August 31, [[Lieutenant Governor of Alaska|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Nancy Dahlstrom]] declined to certify Taylor, temporarily elevating his running mate, Candice English, to the gubernatorial nomination; English subsequently selected Taylor's wife, Jodi Taylor, as her running mate.<ref name="Taylor">{{cite web|url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/08/31/pressure-grows-for-a-consolidated-gop-field-in-alaska-governors-race-as-deadline-nears/|title=Treg Taylor disqualified from ballot as pressure grows for consolidated governor's race|first=Iris|last=Samuels|date=August 31, 2026|work=[[Anchorage Daily News]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260831200254/https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/08/31/pressure-grows-for-a-consolidated-gop-field-in-alaska-governors-race-as-deadline-nears/|archive-date=August 31, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>  On September 4, Dahlstrom reversed her decision and announced that Taylor would be certified after a preliminary review by the Alaska Department of Law raised questions about whether the financial-disclosure requirements had been applied consistently.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Samuels |first=Iris |title=Treg Taylor is back in Alaska's race for governor after election officials reverse decision |url=https://www.adn.com/politics/2026/09/04/treg-taylor-is-back-in-alaskas-race-for-governor-after-election-officials-reverse-decision/ |access-date=2026-09-05 |website=Anchorage Daily News}}</ref>

{{Ifexist not redirect|2026 Arizona gubernatorial election|{{Main|2026 Arizona gubernatorial election}}}}
Governor [[Katie Hobbs]], a Democrat, was elected in [[2022 Arizona gubernatorial election|2022]] with 50.3% of the vote. Starting with this election cycle, gubernatorial candidates will be required to nominate a running mate for the newly established office of [[Lieutenant Governor of Arizona|Lieutenant Governor]]. Hobbs is running for re-election to a second term<ref name="Hobbs">{{cite news |last1=Govidarao |first1=Sejal |title=Democratic Arizona Gov. Hobbs launches reelection bid as her party aims to build power nationally |url=https://apnews.com/article/arizona-governor-katie-hobbs-election-democrat-2b344c58a85ba98e232f4e9d45f41795 |access-date=October 8, 2025 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=October 8, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> and is the nominee, as no other candidates successfully filed for the Democratic primary.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=2026 Arizona Primary Candidates|url=https://apps.arizona.vote/electioninfo/Election/68|website=Arizona Secretary of State}}</ref> 

[[United States Representative|U.S. Representative]] from Arizona's 5th congressional district [[Andy Biggs]]<ref name="Biggs">{{Cite news |work=[[KJZZ-TV]] |access-date=January 31, 2025 |author=Schutsky, Wayne |date=January 27, 2025 |url=https://www.kjzz.org/politics/2025-01-27/congressman-andy-biggs-officially-enters-2026-arizona-governors-race |title=Congressman Andy Biggs officially enters 2026 Arizona governor's race }}</ref> defeated U.S. Representative from Arizona's 1st congressional district [[David Schweikert]],<ref name=Schweikert>{{cite news |last1=Barchenger |first1=Stacey |title=Rep. David Schweikert to run for Arizona governor |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/politics/elections/2025/09/30/david-schweikert-announces-run-for-arizona-governor/86426620007/ |access-date=September 30, 2025 |work=The Arizona Republic|date=September 30, 2025}}</ref> as well as business owner Ken Miceli<ref name=":1" /> and concrete plumbing contractor Scott Neely<ref name="signals">{{cite news |author=Gersony, Laura|date=January 21, 2024|title=US Rep. Andy Biggs signals he is considering run for Arizona governor in 2026|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/politics/arizona/2025/01/21/us-rep-andy-biggs-signals-run-az-governor-2026/77854990007/|access-date=January 21, 2023|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]}}</ref> with 74% of the vote in the Republican primary. 

Healthcare entrepreneur Hugh Lytle and Teri Hourihan are running in the No Labels/[[Arizona Independent Party]] primary. Former Democratic state representative [[Leezah Sun]] has announced a campaign as an independent, but will not appear on the ballot.<ref name="LeezahSun">{{cite news |last1=Fischer |first1=Howie |title=Former Democratic lawmaker Leezah Sun to run for Arizona governor as independent |url=https://azcapitoltimes.com/news/2025/12/23/former-democratic-lawmaker-leezah-sun-to-run-for-arizona-governor-as-independent/ |access-date=December 24, 2025 |work=[[Arizona Capitol Times]] |date=December 23, 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ballotpedia.org/Leezah_Sun|title=Leezah Sun|website=Ballotpedia}}</ref>

This will be the first gubernatorial election in which a candidate is required to select a [[running mate]], following the passage of Proposition 131 in the [[2022 Arizona elections|2022 elections]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barchenger |first=Stacey |title=Arizona will elect its first lieutenant governor in 2026. What to know about the role |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/politics/arizona/2023/09/21/arizona-will-elect-its-first-lieutenant-governor-in-2026-what-to-know/70848159007/ |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=The Arizona Republic |language=en-US}}</ref>

Governor [[Sarah Huckabee Sanders]], a Republican, was elected in [[2022 Arkansas gubernatorial election|2022]] with 63.1% of the vote. She is seeking re-election to a second term and ran unopposed for the Republican nomination.<ref name="SHS2026">{{cite news |last1=Barrow |first1=Bill |title=Project 2028: GOP officials jockey during Republican National Convention for future White House runs |url=https://apnews.com/article/donald-trump-future-republican-candidates-253224301e5730b4309f97b1971b2fb4 |access-date=August 3, 2024 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |date=July 18, 2024 |quote=[Sarah Huckabee Sanders] was focused only on Trump's election and then her own reelection in 2026 |archive-date=August 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240803045038/https://apnews.com/article/donald-trump-future-republican-candidates-253224301e5730b4309f97b1971b2fb4 |url-status=live }}</ref> 

[[Arkansas Senate|State senator]] [[Fredrick Love]]<ref name="LoveAR">{{cite news |last1=Brock |first1=Roby |title=Democratic State Sen. Fred Love announces for Arkansas Governor |url=https://talkbusiness.net/2025/06/democratic-state-sen-fred-love-announces-for-arkansas-governor/ |access-date=June 23, 2025 |work=Talk Business & Politics |date=June 23, 2025}}</ref> defeated former [[Walmart]] executive Supha Xayprasith Mays<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wickline |first1=Michael R. |title=Bentonville businesswoman running again for governor |url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2025/oct/28/bentonville-businesswoman-running-again-for/ |access-date=November 3, 2025 |work=[[Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |date=October 28, 2025}}</ref> in the Democratic primary on March 3, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arkansas Election Night Reporting |url=https://enr.totalresults.com/arkansas#election=7f77a178-af02-40ec-92db-c5cc50882c68&contest=32eedf4d-f628-4868-8ddc-10b83bdd8030&filter=Statewide&bucket=results |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=enr.totalresults.com}}</ref>

[[Farmer]] Colt Shelby is running in the general election as a [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brock |first=Roby |date=2026-02-23 |title=Arkansas Libertarians nominate candidates for 2026 |url=https://talkbusiness.net/2026/02/arkansas-libertarians-nominate-candidates-for-2026/ |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=Talk Business & Politics |language=en-US}}</ref>

{{Main|2026 California gubernatorial election}}
{{See also|2026 California lieutenant gubernatorial election}}
Democratic Governor [[Gavin Newsom]] was re-elected in [[2022 California gubernatorial election|2022]] with 59.2% of the vote. He is term-limited by the [[Constitution of California|California Constitution]] in 2026, and cannot seek re-election to a third term. More than sixty candidates appeared on the June 2026 primary ballot. Democrat [[Xavier Becerra]],<ref name="beccera">{{cite web |last1=Mason |first1=Melanie |title=Xavier Becerra announces bid for California governor|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/04/02/xavier-becerra-announces-bid-for-california-governor-00265564 |publisher=[[Politico]] |date=April 2, 2024 |access-date=April 2, 2024}}</ref> former [[U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services]] and former [[California Attorney General]], and Republican [[Pundit|political commentator]] [[Steve Hilton]]<ref name="HiltonCA">{{cite news |title=Steve Hilton, former David Cameron adviser, to run for California governor |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/apr/23/steve-hilton-former-david-cameron-adviser-to-run-for-california-governor|work=[[The Guardian]] |date=April 23, 2025}}</ref> advanced to the general election.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=CANDIDATES FOR JUNE 2, 2026, PRIMARY ELECTION|url=https://elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov/statewide-elections/2026-primary/governor.pdf|access-date=March 21, 2025|website=State of California Secretary of State}}</ref> 

Other Democratic candidates included [[San Jose, California|San Jose]] [[Mayor of San Jose, California|mayor]] [[Matt Mahan]];<ref name="Mahan">{{Cite web |last=Gardiner |first=Dustin |date=2026-01-29 |title=San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan enters crowded race for California governor |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/01/29/san-jose-mayor-matt-mahan-runs-for-california-governor-00750168 |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=POLITICO |language=en}}</ref> former congresswoman for California's 47th congressional district [[Katie Porter]];<ref name="porterCA">{{Cite news |access-date=March 11, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |date=March 11, 2025 |last=Mason |first=Melanie |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/03/11/katie-porter-enters-california-governors-race-00223194 |title=Katie Porter enters race to succeed California Gov. Gavin Newsom }}</ref> businessman and [[2020 United States presidential election|2020]] presidential candidate [[Tom Steyer]];<ref name="steyer">{{Cite news |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/11/19/tom-steyer-enters-california-governor-race-00657624|title=Tom Steyer enters California governor's race |work=[[Politico]] |language=en-US |last=White |first=Jeremy B. |date=November 19, 2025 |access-date=November 19, 2025}}</ref> [[California State Superintendent of Public Instruction|State Superintendent of Public Instruction]] [[Tony Thurmond]];<ref name="thurmondca">{{Cite news |access-date=September 26, 2023 |work=[[KCRA]] |date=September 26, 2023 |last=Flores |first=Hilda |url=https://www.kcra.com/article/state-superintendent-tony-thurmond-officially-announces-run-governor/45322329 |title=State Superintendent Tony Thurmond officially announces run for governor |archive-date=September 26, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230926191821/https://www.kcra.com/article/state-superintendent-tony-thurmond-officially-announces-run-governor/45322329 |url-status=live }}</ref> and former Los Angeles Mayor [[Antonio Villaraigosa]].<ref name="avca">{{cite web |last1=Gans |first1=Jared |title=Former LA Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa again running for California governor |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/4788052-antonio-villaraigosa-run-california-governor/ |work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |access-date=July 23, 2024 |date=July 23, 2024 |archive-date=July 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240723192527/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/4788052-antonio-villaraigosa-run-california-governor/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

U.S. representative [[Eric Swalwell]] initially announced a campaign in November 2025, but withdrew and resigned from Congress in April 2026 amid sexual assault allegations, with his name still on the ballot.<ref name="swalwellca">{{cite news |access-date=November 21, 2025 |work=[[New York Times]] |date=November 21, 2025 |last=Rosenhall |first=Laurel |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/21/us/eric-swalwell-california-governor.html |title=A Former Trump Impeachment Manager Will Run for California Governor}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |access-date=April 13, 2026 |work=[[CNBC]] |date=April 13, 2026 |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/13/eric-swalwell-resigns-congress.html?msockid=29cacfc12e3f6f8d392cdb5d2fa66ea0 |title=Rep. Eric Swalwell resigns from U.S. House after sexual misconduct allegations}}</ref> Former [[California State Controller|state Controller]] [[Betty Yee]] also withdrew from the race in April 2026 and will remain on the ballot.<ref name="Yee">{{cite web|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/politics/article/betty-yee-california-governor-2026-17916212.php|title=Former California Controller Betty Yee says she will run to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom in 2026|last=Bollag|first=Sophia|date=April 24, 2023|access-date=April 24, 2023|website=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|archive-date=April 25, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230425010118/https://www.sfchronicle.com/politics/article/betty-yee-california-governor-2026-17916212.php|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kcra.com/article/california-governor-betty-yee-suspends-campaign/71075349|title=Former State Controller Betty Yee suspends California governor campaign|last=Ayestas|first=Jonathan|date=April 20, 2026|access-date=April 20, 2026|website=KCRA}}</ref>

Former [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] of the United States and [[2024 United States presidential election|2024]] Democratic nominee for President [[Kamala Harris]] had considered running,<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 8, 2025 |title=Kamala Harris Considering Run for California Governor – The Positive Community |url=https://thepositivecommunity.com/2025/03/08/kamala-harris-considering-run-for-california-governor/ |access-date=March 22, 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref> but ultimately decided not to enter the race.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rosenhall |first=Linda |date=July 30, 2025 |title=Kamala Harris Will Not Run for California Governor in 2026 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/07/30/us/politics/harris-california-governor-race.html |access-date=July 30, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en}}</ref>

Other Republican candidates included [[Riverside County, California|Riverside County]] Sheriff [[Chad Bianco]],<ref name="Bianco">{{cite news |last1=Horseman |first1=Jeff |title=Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco announces California governor run in 2026 |url=https://www.sgvtribune.com/2025/02/17/riverside-county-sheriff-chad-bianco-announces-california-governor-run-in-2026/ |access-date=February 17, 2025 |work=San Gabriel Valley Tribune |date=February 17, 2025}}</ref> diplomat Tim Nelson and businessman Leo Zacky.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-12 |title=Who's running for CA governor to replace termed-out Gavin Newsom? Here's a look at field - so far |url=https://abc7news.com/post/california-governors-race-running-replace-termed-gavin-newsom-heres-look/16009625/ |access-date=2026-03-22 |website=ABC7 San Francisco |language=en}}</ref>

[[Butch Ware]], the [[Green Party of the United States|Green Party]]'s [[2024 United States presidential election|2024]] vice presidential nominee, announced his candidacy but did not meet the requirements to appear on the primary ballot and instead ran as a [[write-in candidate]].<ref name="Ware">{{Cite press release |url=https://www.gp.org/butch_ware_announces_next_run_for_office |title=Butch Ware, former Green Party VP nominee, announces next run for office |date=November 11, 2024 |access-date=November 13, 2024 |work=Green Party of the United States}}</ref>

{{Main|2026 Colorado gubernatorial election}}

Governor [[Jared Polis]], a Democrat, was re-elected in [[2022 Colorado gubernatorial election|2022]] with 58.5% of the vote. He will be term-limited by the [[Colorado Constitution]] in 2026 and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term. 

[[Attorney General of Colorado|State Attorney General]] [[Phil Weiser]]<ref name=Weiser>{{cite news |last=Paul |first=Jesse |access-date=January 2, 2025 |title=Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser launches 2026 campaign for governor |date=January 2, 2025 |url=https://coloradosun.com/2025/01/02/phil-weiser-colorado-governor-2026/}}</ref> defeated [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Michael Bennet]]<ref name="Bennet Announcement">{{cite web |last1=Kim |first1=Caitlyn |title=Sen. Michael Bennet is officially running for governor|url=https://www.cpr.org/2025/04/11/michael-bennet-running-for-colorado-governor/ |website=[[Colorado Public Radio]] |access-date=April 11, 2025 |date=April 11, 2025}}</ref> for the Democratic nomination. 

On the Republican side, ministry leader [[Victor Marx]] defeated state representative [[Scott Bottoms]] and state senator [[Barbara Kirkmeyer]] for the nomination.<ref name="BottomsCO">{{Cite web |last=Paul |first=Jesse |access-date=January 21, 2025 |title=Scott Bottoms, Republican state representative, will run for Colorado governor in 2026 |date=January 20, 2025 |url=https://coloradosun.com/2025/01/20/scott-bottoms-colorado-governor-2026/}}</ref><ref name="KirkmeyerCO">{{cite news |last1=Paul |first1=Jesse |title=Republican Barbara Kirkmeyer is running to be Colorado's next governor |url=https://coloradosun.com/2025/09/09/barbara-kirkmeyer-colorado-governor-2026/ |access-date=September 9, 2025 |work=The Colorado Sun |date=September 9, 2025}}</ref>

Former [[U.S. Representative]] for Colorado's 4th congressional district [[Greg Lopez]] initially announced his campaign as a Republican but later left the party in January 2026 and is continuing his campaign as an independent.<ref name="LopezCO">{{cite news |last1=Metzger |first1=Hannah |title=Lopez launches third Republican run for Colorado governor |url=https://www.9news.com/article/news/local/local-politics/greg-lopez-colorado-governor-candidate-republican/73-74af91fa-7429-451d-bdad-88d5c509c3b9 |access-date=April 14, 2025 |work=9News |date=April 14, 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="LopezInd">{{cite news |last1=Paul |first1=Jesse |title=Major shake-up in crowded Republican primary for Colorado governor as one candidate leaves race, another leaves GOP |url=https://coloradosun.com/2026/01/05/mark-baisley-greg-lopez-colorado-governors-race/ |access-date=January 7, 2026 |work=The Colorado Sun |date=January 5, 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

{{Main|2026 Connecticut gubernatorial election}}

[[List of governors of Connecticut|Governor]] [[Ned Lamont]], a Democrat, was re-elected in [[2022 Connecticut gubernatorial election|2022]] with 56% of the vote. Because [[Connecticut]] does not have gubernatorial term limits in its [[Constitution of Connecticut|Constitution]], Lamont has announced that he is running for a third term.<ref name=Lamont>{{cite news |last=Cerulli|first=Mike|access-date=November 7, 2025 |title= Ned Lamont to run for third term as Connecticut governor in 2026: Sources|date=November 7, 2025 |url=https://www.wtnh.com/news/elections/ned-lamont-to-run-for-third-term-as-connecticut-governor-in-2026-sources/}}</ref> Lamont fended off a primary challenge from [[Connecticut House of Representatives|State representative]] for the 88th district [[Josh Elliott (politician)|Josh Elliott]].<ref name=Pazniokas>{{cite news |last=Pazniokas|first=Mark |access-date=July 11, 2025 |title= Rep. Josh Elliott files to challenge Lamont for governor|date=July 8, 2025 |url=https://ctmirror.org/2025/07/08/rep-josh-elliott-files-to-challenge-lamont-for-governor/}}</ref>

[[Connecticut State Senate|State senator]] for the 36th district [[Ryan Fazio]] is the Republican nominee.<ref name="Fazio">{{cite news |title=Sen. Ryan Fazio announces run for governor in 2026 |url=https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/politics/sen-ryan-fazio-announces-run-for-governor-in-2026/3624953/ |access-date=August 13, 2025 |work=NBC Connecticut |date=August 13, 2025}}</ref> Former [[lieutenant governor of New York]] [[Betsy McCaughey]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=State |first=Luke Parsnow New York |title=Former New York lieutenant governor announces run for governor of Connecticut |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/central-ny/politics/2026/01/15/betsy-mccaughey-announces-run-for-governor-in-connecticut |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=spectrumlocalnews.com |language=en}}</ref>initially announced her candidacy for the Republican nomination in March 2026 but withdrew after not receiving 15% of the convention vote in May. New Britain mayor [[Erin Stewart]] initially ran but dropped out of the race in May 2026, after allegations of misconduct during her tenure as mayor.<ref name="StewartCT">{{cite news |last1=Pazniokas |first1=Mark |title=Erin Stewart kicks off campaign for CT governor |url=https://ctmirror.org/2025/11/18/erin-stewart-kicks-off-campaign-for-ct-governor/ |access-date=November 18, 2025 |work=[[The Connecticut Mirror]] |date=November 18, 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Republican Erin Stewart suspends campaign for Connecticut governor amid report of misconduct |url=https://www.ctinsider.com/politics/article/erin-stewart-suspends-campaign-governor-fazio-22258746.php |date=May 14, 2026|author=Putterman, Alex|website=ctinsider.com}}</ref>
{{clear}}

Republican Governor [[Ron DeSantis]] was re-elected in [[2022 Florida gubernatorial election|2022]] with 59.4% of the vote. He is term-limited by the [[Constitution of Florida|Florida Constitution]] in 2026 and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term.

[[U.S. representative]] for Florida's 19th congressional district [[Byron Donalds]] announced his candidacy on February 25, 2025, becoming the first major Republican to enter the race.<ref name="Burkett">{{cite news |last1=Scheckner |first1=Jesse |title=Charles Burkett, Surfside's 4-term Mayor, says he's running for Governor |url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/729249-charles-burkett-surfsides-3-time-mayor-says-hes-running-for-governor/ |access-date=March 31, 2025 |work=[[Florida Politics]] |date=March 31, 2025}}</ref> [[Paul Renner (politician)|Paul Renner]], former [[List of speakers of the Florida House of Representatives|Speaker of the Florida House of Representatives]], announced his candidacy in September 2025, and Lieutenant Governor [[Jay Collins]] joined the race in January 2026.<ref name="Renner">{{cite web |last1=Dixon |first1=Matt |title=Second big-name Republican jumps into the race to replace Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis|url=https://floridianpress.com/2025/07/paul-renner-told-desantis-he-wants-to-run-for-governor/ |publisher=[[NBC News]] |access-date=3 September 2025 |date=3 September 2025}}</ref><ref name="CollinsFL">{{Cite web |last=Shepard |first=Skyler |date=2026-01-12 |title=Jay Collins, Green Beret turned lieutenant governor, announces run for Florida governor |url=https://cbs12.com/news/local/jay-collins-green-beret-turned-lieutenant-governor-announces-run-for-florida-governor-florida-news-leadership-forged-under-pressure-not-in-soundbites-us-rep-byron-donalds-january-12-2026 |access-date=2026-01-12 |website=WPEC |language=en}}</ref> Other Republican candidates include [[Surfside, Florida|Surfside]] mayor Charles Burkett and entrepreneur [[James Fishback]].<ref name="Burkett" /><ref name="Fishback">{{cite news |last1=Cai |first1=Sophia |last2=Leonard |first2=Kimberly |title=Pro-DeSantis candidate James Fishback launching bid for Florida governor |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/11/10/pro-desantis-candidate-james-fishback-launching-bid-for-florida-governor-00645553 |access-date=November 11, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |date=November 10, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> 

Former Republican U.S. representative for [[Florida's 13th congressional district]] [[David Jolly]], a staunch critic of Trump, joined the Democratic Party in 2025 and announced his candidacy June 2025.<ref name="Jolly">{{Cite web |last=Leonard |first=Kimberly |date=June 5, 2025 |title=Well-known Trump critic David Jolly enters race for Florida governor |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/06/05/david-jolly-enters-race-florida-governor-00386873 |access-date=June 5, 2025 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en}}</ref> [[Orange County, Florida|Orange County]] [[Mayor of Orange County|Mayor]] [[Jerry Demings]] is also running for the Democratic nomination.<ref name="Demings">{{cite web |last1=Rohrer |first1=Gray |title=Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings enters governor race |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/news/politics/2025/11/03/demings-governor-run/87068826007/ |access-date=November 3, 2025 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=November 3, 2025}}</ref>

Former [[Florida Senate|State Senate Minority Leader]] [[Jason Pizzo]] launched an independent bid for governor in May 2025,<ref name="Pizzo">{{cite news |last1=Fineout |first1=Gary |title=After dramatic Democratic Party exit, Pizzo says he's running for Florida governor |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/05/09/pizzo-governor-democratic-party-exit-00340240 |access-date=May 9, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |date=May 9, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> while [[Moliere Dimanche]] announced his own independent campaign in July 2024, becoming the first [[Haiti|Haitian]] candidate for governor in Florida's history.<ref name="auto">{{cite web | title=Moliere Dimanche | url=https://ballotpedia.org/Moliere_Dimanche | website=Ballotpedia | accessdate=December 31, 2024}}</ref>
{{clear}}

{{See also|2026 Georgia lieutenant gubernatorial election}}
Republican [[Governor of Georgia|Governor]] [[Brian Kemp]] was re-elected in [[2022 Georgia gubernatorial election|2022]] with 53.4% of the vote. He is term-limited by the [[Constitution of Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia Constitution]] in 2026 and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term. 

[[Georgia Attorney General|Attorney General]] [[Chris Carr (politician)|Chris Carr]],<ref name="CARR2026">{{cite news |last1=Bluestein |first1=Greg |title=Georgia AG Chris Carr launches GOP campaign for governor, kicking off 2026 race |url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/georgia-ag-chris-carr-enters-2026-race-for-governor-kicking-off-race/UUBZXWHT25GHPNBUVO6RBEKPSA/ |access-date=November 21, 2024 |publisher=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=November 21, 2024}}</ref> [[Lieutenant Governor of Georgia|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Burt Jones]],<ref name="JonesGA">{{Cite news |last=Bluestein |first=Greg |date=July 8, 2025 |title=Burt Jones enters Georgia governor's race with Trump-aligned platform |url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/2025/07/burt-jones-enters-georgia-governors-race-with-trump-aligned-platform/ |access-date=July 8, 2025 |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |language=English |issn=}}</ref> [[Georgia Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Brad Raffensperger]],<ref name="Raffensperger">{{cite news |first1=Joyce |last1=Lupiani |first2=Lindsay |last2=Tuman |work=[[FOX 5 Atlanta]] |access-date=September 17, 2025 |url=https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/brad-raffensperger-announces-run-georgia-governor |date=September 17, 2025 |title=Brad Raffensperger announces run for Georgia governor}}</ref> and healthcare executive [[Rick Jackson (businessman)|Rick Jackson]]<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Bluestein|first1=Greg|title=Republican Rick Jackson enters Georgia governor's race in surprise move|url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/02/surprise-republican-rick-jackson-enters-georgia-governors-race/|date=February 3, 2026|website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]}}</ref> all announced bids for the Republican nomination. Jackson and Jones advanced to a runoff that took place on June 16, which Jackson won, thus becoming the Republican nominee.

On the Democratic side, former [[Mayor of Atlanta]] and former director of the [[White House Office of Public Engagement]] [[Keisha Lance Bottoms]]<ref name="Bottoms">{{Cite web |last=Kamisar |first=Ben |date=May 20, 2025 |title=Former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms launches run for Georgia governor |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/former-atlanta-mayor-keisha-lance-bottoms-launches-run-georgia-governo-rcna207688 |access-date=May 20, 2025 |website=[[NBC News]]}}</ref> became the nominee on May 19 and defeated a crowded field, which included former state senator [[Jason Esteves]],<ref name="Esteves">{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Dave |date=April 21, 2025 |title=Democratic state Sen. Jason Esteves announces election bid to run for Georgia governor |url=https://www.augustachronicle.com/story/news/state/2025/04/21/state-senator-jason-esteves-announces-election-bid-for-georgia-governor/83193844007/ |access-date=April 21, 2025 |website=[[The Augusta Chronicle]]}}</ref> former [[DeKalb County, Georgia|DeKalb County]] Chief Executive Officer and  [[2010 United States Senate election in Georgia|2010]] nominee for U.S. Senate [[Mike Thurmond]],<ref name="ThurmondGA">{{Cite web |last=Amy |first=Jeff |date=August 6, 2025 |title=Democrat Michael Thurmond launches 2026 run for Georgia governor |url=https://apnews.com/article/mike-thurmond-governor-georgia-democrat-333e82505c2eb7ede947d0de5120f92c |access-date=August 6, 2025 |website=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> and state representative [[Derrick Jackson (politician)|Derrick Jackson]].<ref name="DerrickJackson">{{cite news |last1=Mitchell |first1=Tia |title=State Rep. Derrick Jackson is latest Democrat to launch bid for governor |url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/2025/06/state-rep-derrick-jackson-is-latest-democrat-to-launch-bid-for-governor/ |access-date=June 3, 2025 |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=June 3, 2025 |language=English}}</ref> Former Lieutenant Governor [[Geoff Duncan]], a Republican critic of Donald Trump, switched to the Democratic Party and ran for governor.<ref name="Duncan">{{cite news |last1=Schneider |first1=Elena |title=Former Lt. Gov. Geoff Duncan runs for Georgia governor — as a Democrat |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/09/16/former-lt-gov-geoff-duncan-runs-for-georgia-governor-as-a-democrat-00564859 |access-date=September 16, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |date=September 16, 2025 |language=English}}</ref>

[[Governor of Idaho|Governor]] [[Brad Little]], a Republican, was re-elected in [[2022 Idaho gubernatorial election|2022]] with 60.5% of the vote. Because [[Idaho]] does not have gubernatorial term limits in its [[Constitution of Idaho|Constitution]], he is running for re-election to a third term.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-24 |title=Idaho Governor Brad Little announces bid for a third term as state leader |url=https://www.ktvb.com/article/news/local/idaho-governor-announces-bid-for-a-third-term-as-state-leader/277-0d9022d1-8685-4827-a78c-2c62e6d8a40e |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=ktvb.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Former [[Twin Falls, Idaho|Twin Falls]] Transit Coordinator Maxine Durand is running as an independent, with the backing of local branches of the [[Democratic Socialists of America]].<ref name="Durand">{{cite news |last=Dolan |first=Sean |date=August 30, 2025 |title=Twin Falls socialist candidate Maxine Durand running for Idaho Governor |url=https://magicvalley.com/news/local/government-politics/elections/article_33ee90c3-8e0b-4f7b-b6de-8e04b75876c8.html |access-date=September 5, 2025 |work=[[Twin Falls Times-News]] |language=en}}</ref>

Governor [[JB Pritzker]], a Democrat, was re-elected in [[2022 Illinois gubernatorial election|2022]] with 54.9% of the vote and is running for a third term.<ref name=IL2026>{{#invoke:cite|web|title=Candidate Filing Search|url=https://www.elections.il.gov/ElectionOperations/CandidateFilingSearch.aspx?ID=Z2J%2fvYpKX8w%3d|website=Illinois State Board of Elections|access-date=October 27, 2025}}</ref> With Lieutenant Governor [[Juliana Stratton]] seeking Illinois's U.S. Senate seat in [[2026 United States Senate election in Illinois|2026]], Pritzker's running mate is former state representative [[Christian Mitchell]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pritzker Taps Former Deputy Gov. Christian Mitchell as Running Mate |url=https://news.wttw.com/2025/07/01/pritzker-taps-former-deputy-gov-christian-mitchell-running-mate |access-date=2025-09-30 |website=WTTW News|author=Cherone, Heather|date=July 1, 2025}}</ref> Pritzker won the Democratic nomination unopposed.

On the Republican side, former [[Illinois Senate|state senator]] and 2022 Republican nominee for governor [[Darren Bailey]] secured the nomination against former vice president of policy for the [[Illinois Policy Institute]] Ted Dabrowski, [[DuPage County, Illinois|DuPage County]] Sheriff James Mendrick, and real estate developer Rick Heidner.<ref name="IL2026" />

{{Ifexist not redirect|2026 Iowa gubernatorial election|{{Main|2026 Iowa gubernatorial election}}}}
Governor [[Kim Reynolds]], a Republican, was re-elected in [[2022 Iowa gubernatorial election|2022]] with 58.1% of the vote. While she is eligible to run for re-election to a third full term, she has decided not to run.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crisp |first1=Elizabeth |title=Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds won't seek a third term |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/5244795-iowa-gov-reynolds-announcement/?tbref=hp |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |access-date=April 11, 2025 |date=April 11, 2025}}</ref> 

Republican candidates included state representative [[Eddie Andrews (American politician)|Eddie Andrews]],<ref name="AndrewsIA">{{Cite web |last=Pfannenstiel |first=Brianne |title=Republican State Rep. Eddie Andrews files paperwork to run for Iowa governor in 2026 |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2025/06/03/republican-eddie-andrews-iowa-files-paperwork-to-run-for-governor-in-2026/84007787007/ |access-date=June 3, 2025 |website=The Des Moines Register |language=en-US}}</ref> U.S. Representative for Iowa's 4th congressional district [[Randy Feenstra]],<ref name="CBSNews1">{{cite news |last1=Jacobs|first1=Jennifer | last2 = Gomez | first2 = Fin | last3 = Hudak | first3 = Zak|title=Iowa's GOP Rep. Randy Feenstra launches campaign for governor|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/iowa-governors-race-2026-randy-feenstra-rob-sand/|access-date=May 12, 2025 |work=[[CBS News]] |date=May 12, 2025}}</ref> former director of the Iowa Department of Administrative Services Adam Steen,<ref name="Steen">{{cite news |last1=Opsahl |first1=Robin |title=Former Iowa administrator Adam Steen announces GOP campaign for governor |url=https://iowacapitaldispatch.com/2025/08/19/former-iowa-administrator-adam-steen-announces-gop-campaign-for-governor/ |access-date=August 22, 2025 |work=[[Iowa Capital Dispatch]] |date=August 19, 2025}}</ref> businessman Zach Lahn,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gazette |first=Erin Murphy The |date=2026-03-13 |title=Lahn traveling different path in search of Iowa GOP gubernatorial nomination |url=https://www.thegazette.com/news/politics/lahn-traveling-different-path-in-search-of-iowa-gop-gubernatorial-nomination/article_158bda32-fb0c-4c2f-afc2-cf601c79f843.html |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=The Gazette |language=en}}</ref> and former state representative [[Brad Sherman (Iowa politician)|Brad Sherman]].<ref name="ShermanIA">{{cite news |last1=Pfannenstiel |first1=Brianne |title=Former Republican state representative to challenge Kim Reynolds for Iowa governor seat |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2025/02/17/republican-brad-sherman-to-run-for-iowa-governor-against-incumbent-kim-reynolds-gop/78963619007/ |access-date=February 17, 2025 |work=[[The Des Moines Register]] |date=February 17, 2025}}</ref> Zach Lahn won the nomination on June 2, in what was considered a major upset.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Knowles |first1=Hannah  |last2=Allison |first2=Natalie |title=Trump's pick for Iowa governor loses GOP primary in upset |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/06/03/trumps-pick-iowa-governor-concedes-gop-primary-upset/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=June 3, 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

On the Democratic side, [[State Auditor of Iowa|State Auditor]] [[Rob Sand]] declared his candidacy in May 2025 and won the nomination as the only candidate to file by the deadline. He is also the only [[Iowa Democratic Party |Democratic]] statewide officeholder in Iowa.<ref name="SandIA">{{cite news |last1=Tallal |first1=Skylar |title=Iowa Auditor Rob Sand announces 2026 gubernatorial run |url=https://cbs2iowa.com/news/local/iowa-auditor-rob-sand-announces-2026-gubernatorial-run-governor-kim-reynolds-republicans-democrats |access-date=May 12, 2025 |work=KGAN |date=May 12, 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

{{Ifexist not redirect|2026 Kansas gubernatorial election|{{Main|2026 Kansas gubernatorial election}}}}
Governor [[Laura Kelly]], a Democrat, was re-elected in [[2022 Kansas gubernatorial election|2022]] with 49.5% of the vote. She will be term limited  by the [[Kansas Constitution]] and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term. 

State senators [[Ethan Corson]]<ref name="Corson">{{cite web|url=http://www.kslegislature.org/li/b2021_22/members/sen_corson_ethan_1/|title=Senator Ethan Corson |publisher=Kslegislature.org |access-date=January 13, 2021}}</ref> and [[Cindy Holscher]]<ref name="Holscher">{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Sherman |title=Democrat steps forward in race for Kansas governor, focuses on schools and 'kitchen table' issues |url=https://kansasreflector.com/2025/06/12/democrat-steps-forward-in-race-for-kansas-governor-focuses-on-schools-and-kitchen-table-issues/ |access-date=June 12, 2025 |work=[[Kansas Reflector]] |date=June 12, 2025}}</ref> ran for the Democratic nomination, with Corson receiving Governor Kelly's endorsement.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 22, 2025 |title=Gov. Kelly endorses state senator Ethan Corson as he launches gubernatorial campaign |url=https://www.kake.com/home/gov-kelly-endorses-state-senator-ethan-corson-as-he-launches-gubernatorial-campaign/article_2b3eab4d-ea75-4e71-804c-36c0ca54a926.html |access-date=August 15, 2025 |website=KAKE |language=en}}</ref> Holscher defeated Corson with 48.8% of the vote on August 4. 

Candidates for the Republican nomination included State Senate President [[Ty Masterson]], Kansas Insurance Commissioner [[Vicki Schmidt]], Kansas Secretary of State [[Scott Schwab]], and [[Johnson County, Kansas|Johnson County]] Commissioner [[Charlotte O'Hara]].<ref name="Collyer">{{cite news |author=Robinson, Colter|date=May 14, 2025 |work=[[KSNT]] |access-date=May 14, 2025 |url=https://www.ksnt.com/capitol-bureau/dr-jeff-colyer-announces-bid-for-kansas-governor/ |title=Dr. Jeff Colyer announces bid for Kansas governor}}</ref><ref name="Schwab">{{cite news |last1=Robinson |first1=Colter |title=Scott Schwab announces run for Kansas Governor |url=https://www.ksnt.com/news/local-news/scott-schwab-announces-run-for-kansas-governor/ |access-date=January 8, 2025 |work=KSNT |date=January 8, 2025}}</ref><ref name="O'Hara">{{cite news |author=Hammill, Roxie |date=March 10, 2025 |work=[[Johnson County Post]] |access-date=March 11, 2025 |url=https://johnsoncountypost.com/2025/03/10/charlotte-ohara-kansas-governor-bid-254803/ |title=Former JoCo commissioner Charlotte O'Hara announces bid for governor}}</ref> Masterson won the Republican nomination on August 4 with 43.2% of the vote.

Governor [[Janet Mills]], a Democrat, was re-elected in [[2022 Maine gubernatorial election|2022]] with 55.4% of the vote. She will be term-limited by the [[Maine Constitution]], and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term. 

Former State House Speaker [[Hannah Pingree]], the daughter of U.S. Representative [[Chellie Pingree]]<ref name="Pingree">{{cite news |last1=Pendharkar |first1=Eesha |title=Hannah Pingree officially launches bid for governor |url=https://mainemorningstar.com/briefs/hannah-pingree-officially-launches-run-for-governor/ |access-date=June 10, 2025 |work=[[Maine Morning Star]] |date=June 10, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> defeated a crowded Democratic field, which included Secretary of State [[Shenna Bellows]];<ref name="Bellows">{{Cite web |last=Kobin |first=Billy |date=March 26, 2025 |title=Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows will run for governor in 2026 |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2025/03/26/politics/state-politics/maine-secretary-of-state-shenna-bellows-will-run-for-governor-2026-joam40zk0w/ |access-date=March 26, 2025 |website=Bangor Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> former State Senate President [[Troy Jackson]];<ref name="TroyDale">{{cite news |last1=Hilton |first1=AnnMarie |title=Former Senate President Troy Jackson enters race for governor |url=https://mainemorningstar.com/briefs/former-senate-president-troy-jackson-enters-race-for-governor/ |access-date=May 19, 2025 |work=Maine Morning Star |ref=May 19, 2025}}</ref> businessman [[Angus King III]], the son of independent U.S. Senator and former Maine governor [[Angus King]];<ref name="AngusIII">{{Cite web |last=Everett |first=Burgess |date=May 6, 2025 |title=King of Maine? Angus King III launches governor bid |url=https://www.semafor.com/article/05/06/2025/king-of-maine-angus-king-iii-launches-governor-bid |website=Semafor}}</ref> and former [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] principal deputy director [[Nirav D. Shah|Dr. Nirav Shah]].<ref name="ShahME">{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Kevin |title=Former Maine CDC Director Dr. Nirav Shah Joins Democratic Race for Governor|url=https://www.mainepublic.org/politics/2025-10-20/former-maine-cdc-director-dr-nirav-shah-joins-democratic-race-for-governor |access-date=June 10, 2025 |work=[[Maine Public Broadcasting Network]] |date=October 20, 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

On the Republican side, former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State [[Robert B. Charles|Robert Charles]]<ref name="CharlesME">{{Cite web |last=Kobin |first=Billy |date=April 15, 2025 |title=He served under George W. Bush. Now he's running for Maine governor. |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2025/04/15/politics/elections/maine-election-2026-republican-governor-candidate-bobby-charles/ |access-date=April 15, 2025 |website=Bangor Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> defeated a field which included healthcare executive and member of the Bush family [[Jonathan S. Bush|Jonathan Bush]];<ref name="BushME">{{Cite web |last=Reed |first=Russ |date=2025-10-08 |title=Jonathan Bush announces he's running for governor of Maine |url=https://www.wmtw.com/article/jonathan-bush-maine-governor-campaign-launch/68910077 |access-date=2025-10-08 |website=WMTW |language=en}}</ref> real estate businessman David Jones;<ref name="JonesME">{{cite news |last1=Cover |first1=Susan |title=Falmouth Republican launches bid for Maine governor in 2026 |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/me/maine/politics/2025/05/20/falmouth-republican-launches-bid-for-maine-governor-in-2026 |access-date=May 20, 2025 |work=[[Spectrum News]] |date=May 20, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> [[Maine Senate|state senator]] and candidate for governor in [[2002 Maine gubernatorial election|2002]] [[James Libby]];<ref name="LibbyME">{{cite news |last1=St Pierre |first1=Ariana |title=Sen. James Libby running for governor of Maine |url=https://wgme.com/news/local/sen-james-libby-running-for-governor-of-maine-republicans-democrats-shenna-bellows-troy-jackson-angus-king-iii-david-jones-janet-mills |access-date=May 22, 2025 |work=[[WGME-TV]] |date=May 22, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> former Maine Senate majority leader and candidate for governor in [[2018 Maine gubernatorial election|2018]] [[Garrett Mason]];<ref name="MasonME">{{Cite web |last=Shepherd |first=Michael |date=2026-01-07 |title=Garrett Mason runs for Maine governor with the help of a top JD Vance ally |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/01/07/politics/elections/garrett-mason-runs-for-maine-governor-joam40zk0w/ |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=Bangor Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> entrepreneur Owen McCarthy;<ref name="McCarthyME">{{cite news |title=Businessman Owen McCarthy joins Gubernatorial race |url=https://www.wabi.tv/2025/06/11/businessman-owen-mccarthy-joins-gubernatorial-race/ |access-date=June 11, 2025 |work=[[WABI-TV]] |date=June 11, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> businessman Ben Midgley;<ref name="Midgley">{{cite news |last1=Kobin |first1=Billy |title=Former fitness executive Ben Midgley joins Maine Republican governor's race |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2025/08/05/politics/elections/maine-ben-midgley-republican-election-2026-governor-race/ |access-date=August 6, 2025 |work=Bangor Daily News |date=August 5, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> and former [[Paris, Maine|Paris]] selectman Robert Wessels.<ref name="Wessels">{{cite web |title=Wessels declares gubernatorial candidacy plans to scooter across state|url=https://www.sunjournal.com/2024/04/25/oxford-hills-man-scootering-across-maine/|publisher=[[Sun Journal (Lewiston, Maine)|Sun Journal]]|access-date=November 17, 2024|date=April 25, 2024}}</ref>

Pingree and Charles will be joined on the ballot by independent state senator [[Rick Bennett (politician)|Rick Bennett]], who left the Republican Party shortly before launching his campaign.<ref name="BennettMaine">{{cite news |title=State Sen. Rick Bennett launches gubernatorial campaign for 2026 |url=https://www.newscentermaine.com/article/news/politics/maine-politics/republican-state-senator-rick-bennet-run-for-maine-governor-2026-independent-candidate/97-575d0eb1-e965-417c-a5b1-217d0ad441f3 |access-date=June 24, 2025 |work=[[WCSH]]|date=June 24, 2025}}</ref>

Governor [[Wes Moore]], a Democrat, was elected in [[2022 Maryland gubernatorial election|2022]] with 64.5% of the vote. He is running for re-election to a second term.<ref name="MooreMD">{{cite news |last1=Cox |first1=Erin |title=Gov. Wes Moore tamps down presidential talk, launches reelection bid |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2025/09/09/wes-moore-reelection-announcement-trump-spat/ |access-date=September 9, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=September 9, 2025}}</ref> Moore easily defeated physician Eric Felber in the Democratic primary.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Elections |url=https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/Primary_candidates/2026_GP_statewide_candidatelist.html |access-date=2026-03-25 |website=elections.maryland.gov}}</ref> 

A number of Republicans are vying for the party's nomination: businessman Carl Brunner,<ref name="MD2024">{{cite web |title=2026 Candidate Listing |url=https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/Primary_candidates/gen_cand_lists_2026_1.html |website=elections.maryland.gov |publisher=Maryland State Board of Elections |access-date=July 30, 2025}}</ref> former state delegate and 2022 nominee [[Dan Cox]],<ref name="CoxMD">{{cite news |last1=Marshall |first1=Ryan |title=Cox files to run for Md. governor, with Krop as running mate |url=https://www.fredericknewspost.com/news/politics_and_government/elections/cox-files-to-run-for-md-governor-with-krop-as-running-mate/article_e93bc106-82b7-510c-bb06-cfd3232c506d.html |access-date=January 30, 2026 |work=[[The Frederick News-Post]] |date=January 30, 2026 |language=en}}</ref> businessman [[Ed Hale (businessman)|Ed Hale]],<ref name="HaleGOPMD">{{cite news |last1=Wood |first1=Pamela |title=Ed Hale Sr. to switch parties, run for governor as a Republican |url=https://www.thebanner.com/politics-power/state-government/ed-hale-republican-governor-maryland-MIPKLZUXPRHKHPZLDO2J4LWGWM/ |access-date=August 20, 2025 |work=The Baltimore Banner |date=August 20, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> and John Myrick, a candidate for U.S. Senate in [[2024 United States Senate election in Maryland|2024]], have announced their candidacies for governor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sears |first=Bryan P. |date=May 1, 2025 |title=Early GOP candidate for governor taps former delegate as running mate |url=https://marylandmatters.org/2025/05/01/early-gop-candidate-for-governor-taps-former-delegate-as-running-mate/ |access-date=May 20, 2025 |website=Maryland Matters |language=en-US}}</ref> Cox became the Republican nominee on June 23.

Democratic Governor [[Gretchen Whitmer]] was re-elected in [[2022 Michigan gubernatorial election|2022]] with 54.5% of the vote. She is term-limited by the [[Constitution of Michigan|Michigan Constitution]] in 2026 and cannot seek re-election to a third term. 

Secretary of State [[Jocelyn Benson]] and [[Genessee County, Michigan|Genessee County]] Sheriff Chris Swanson announced campaigns for the Democratic nomination.<ref name=Benson>{{Cite web |last=Foster |first=Wells |title=Foster: REPORT: Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson 'accidentally' announces run for governor on social media |url=https://www.wilx.com/2025/01/22/report-secretary-state-jocelyn-benson-accidentally-announces-run-governor/|access-date=January 21, 2025 |website=The Detroit News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=Swanson>{{Cite web |last=Cappelletti |first=Joey |title=Chris Swanson, prominent sheriff and Democrat, announces run for Michigan governor |url=https://apnews.com/article/michigan-governor-sheriff-swanson-democrat-whitmer-3b77379b64a3b06f2d6043757598d35a|access-date=February 6, 2025 |website=[[The Associated Press]] |date=February 6, 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref> Benson easily defeated Swanson with 83.2% of the vote on August 4 and became the Democratic nominee.

Businessman, 2022 candidate for governor and [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 candidate for president]] [[Perry Johnson (businessman)|Perry Johnson]]; and [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] for Michigan's 10th congressional district and nominee for U.S. Senate in [[2018 United States Senate election in Michigan|2018]] and [[2020 United States Senate election in Michigan|2020]] [[John James (Michigan politician)|John James]] announced bids for the Republican nomination.<ref name="JamesMI" >{{Cite web |last=Powers |first=Sara |date=April 7, 2025 |title=Rep. John James announces run for Michigan governor |url=https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/local/2025/04/07/rep-john-james-announces-run-for-michigan-governor/ |access-date=April 7, 2025 |website=WDIV |language=en}}</ref> James defeated Johnson with 50.1% of the vote on August 4.

Detroit mayor [[Mike Duggan]], a former Democrat, announced his intention to run for governor as an independent in December 2024.<ref name="Duggan">{{cite web |title=Detroit Mayor Duggan, a longtime Democrat, will run for Michigan governor in 2026 as independent |first=Corey |last=Williams |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 4, 2024 |access-date=December 7, 2024 |url=https://apnews.com/article/duggan-detroit-michigan-governor-independent-democrat-5dba0e7b2d9304c2a00d716c9cd6ca05}}</ref> He suspended his campaign in May 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/05/21/mike-duggan-ends-michigan-governor-campaign-independent/90194635007/|title=Mike Duggan ends 2026 independent campaign for Michigan governor|first=Arpan|last=Lobo|website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref>
{{clear}}

{{Main|2026 Minnesota gubernatorial election}}

Governor [[Tim Walz]], a Democrat, was re-elected in [[2022 Minnesota gubernatorial election|2022]] with 52.3% of the vote. He initially announced a campaign for a third term, but later withdrew his candidacy in January 2026.<ref name="Walz26"/> [[Minnesota]] does not have gubernatorial term limits in its [[Minnesota Constitution|Constitution]].<ref name="Walz">{{Cite web |last=Marquez |first=Alexandra |date=September 16, 2025 |title=Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz will run for a third term in 2026 |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/minnesota-gov-tim-walz-will-run-third-term-2026-rcna229383 |access-date=September 16, 2025 |website=[[NBC News]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Since the adoption of four-year terms in 1962,{{efn|via Constitutional referendum in 1958<ref>{{cite web |title=1957 Session Laws |url=https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1957/0/Session+Law/Chapter/813/pdf/ |website=Office of the Revisor of Statutes |access-date=July 24, 2024 |archive-date=August 14, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240814190758/https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1957/0/Session+Law/Chapter/813/pdf/ |url-status=live }}</ref>}} no Minnesota governor has won a third term. 

Following Walz's announcement of not seeking re-election, [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Amy Klobuchar]] announced a campaign on January 29, 2026.<ref name="Klobuchar">{{cite news |last1=Griffith |first1=Michelle |title=Sen. Klobuchar launches campaign for Minnesota governor |url=https://minnesotareformer.com/2026/01/29/sen-klobuchar-launches-campaign-for-minnesota-governor/ |access-date=January 29, 2026 |work=[[Minnesota Reformer]] |date=January 29, 2026}}</ref> Several other [[Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party|Democratic-Farmer-Labor]] (DFL) candidates filed, none of whom have previously held elected offices in the state. Community organizer Kobey Layne positioned herself as the Progressive candidate and challenged Klobuchar for the DFL's endorsement, but Klobuchar was endorsed in the first ballot alongside her running mate [[Ben Schierer]].<ref name="LayneMN">{{cite news |last1=Griffith |first1=Michelle |title=Klobuchar fights off challenge from left, wins DFL convention nod in bid for governor |url=https://minnesotareformer.com/2026/05/30/klobuchar-fights-off-challenge-from-left-wins-dfl-convention-nod-in-bid-for-governor/ |access-date=3 June 2026 |work=Minnesota Reformer |date=May 30, 2026}}</ref> Klobuchar would then go on to win the Democratic nomination on August 11.

Republican candidates included State House Speaker [[Lisa Demuth]],<ref name="Demuth">{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Lindsey |date=2025-11-02 |title=Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth to announce she's entering the Governor's race |url=https://www.audacy.com/wccoradio/news/local/rep-house-speaker-lisa-demuth-will-enter-governors-race |access-date=2025-11-02 |website=Audacy |language=en-US}}</ref> [[My Pillow]] CEO and conservative activist [[Mike Lindell]],<ref name="Lindell">{{cite news |title=MyPillow's Mike Lindell announces he's running for Minnesota governor as a Republican |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/mike-lindell-minnesota-governor-republican-campaign-mypillow/ |access-date=December 11, 2025 |work=[[CBS Minnesota]] |date=December 11, 2025}}</ref> and healthcare technology executive Kendall Qualls.<ref name="Qualls">{{cite news |last1=Cox |first1=Peter |title=Kendall Qualls enters 2026 Minnesota governor's race as a GOP nomination contender |url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2025/05/08/qualls-makes-second-run-for-minnesota-governor |access-date=May 8, 2025 |work=[[Minnesota Public Radio]] |date=May 8, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Qualls received the Republican Party's endorsement after ten rounds of balloting.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Esme |title=How Kendall Qualls upset Lisa Demuth for the Minnesota GOP governor endorsement |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/kendall-qualls-minnesota-gop-governor-endorsement-lisa-demuth/ |access-date=3 June 2026 |work=CBS Minnesota |date=June 1, 2026}}</ref> Demuth would go on to win the Republican nomination, defeating both Lindell and Qualls.

He is running for re-election to a second term.<ref name="PillenNE">{{cite news |last1=Anderson |first1=Jake |title='Make our great state even greater': Jim Pillen announces reelection bid as Nebraska's governor |url=https://www.ketv.com/article/nebraska-jim-pillen-running-reelection-governor/64916825 |access-date=May 29, 2025 |work=[[KETV]] |date=May 29, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He faced some challenges in the Republican primary, including medicinal cannabis activist Jacy Todd.<ref name="JacyTodd">{{cite news |last1=Wendling |first1=Zach |title=Medical cannabis advocate, targeted notary running for Nebraska governor |url=https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2025/07/08/medical-cannabis-advocate-targeted-notary-running-for-nebraska-governor/ |access-date=July 8, 2025 |work=Nebraska Examiner |date=July 8, 2025}}</ref>

Former [[Nebraska Legislature|state senator]] and [[2018 Nebraska gubernatorial election|2018]] Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor [[Lynne Walz]] is the Democratic nominee.<ref name="WalzNE">{{cite news |last1=Anderson |first1=Jake |title=Former Nebraska state senator Lynne Walz announces campaign for governor |url=https://www.ketv.com/article/nebraska-governor-2026-election-state-senator-campaign/69514033 |access-date=November 24, 2025 |work=[[KETV]] |date=November 24, 2025}}</ref>

Joe Lombardo launches re-election campaign |first1=Kyle |last1=Chouinard |work=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |date=September 15, 2025 |access-date=September 16, 2025 |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2025/sep/15/nevada-gov-joe-lombardo-launches-re-election-campa/}}</ref> Businesswoman Irina Hansen, who ran for [[Mayor of Las Vegas]] in [[2024 Las Vegas mayoral election|2024]], challenged Lombardo in the GOP primary.<ref name="HansenNV">{{cite news |title=Irina Hansen announces candidacy for Nevada governor in 2026 race |url=https://news3lv.com/news/local/irina-hansen-announces-candidacy-for-nevada-governor-in-2026-race |access-date=June 18, 2025 |work=KSNV |date=June 18, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Lombardo easily defeated Hansen with over 90% of the vote on June 9 and became the Republican nominee.

Ford]] defeated [[Washoe County, Nevada|Washoe County]] Commissioner [[Alexis Hill (Nevada politician)|Alexis Hill]] for the Democratic nomination.<ref name="FordNV">{{cite news |last1=Seeman |first1=Matthew |title=Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford formally launches campaign for governor |url=https://news3lv.com/news/local/nevada-attorney-general-aaron-ford-formally-launches-campaign-governor-gubernatorial-democratic-party-politics-joe-lombardo-republican-las-vegas-reno-carson-city |access-date=July 28, 2025 |work=[[KSNV]] |date=July 28, 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/democrat-alexis-hill-jumps-into-nevada-governor-race-unveils-revenue-raising-tax-plan|title=Democrat Alexis Hill jumps into Nevada governor race, unveils revenue-raising tax plan|date=September 4, 2025|website=The Nevada Independent}}</ref>

Governor [[Michelle Lujan Grisham]], a Democrat, was re-elected in [[2022 New Mexico gubernatorial election|2022]] with 52.0% of the vote. She will be term-limited by the [[Constitution of New Mexico|New Mexico Constitution]] in 2026 and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term. 

Former [[United States Secretary of the Interior|U.S. Secretary of the Interior]] and U.S. Representative [[Deb Haaland]] defeated [[Bernalillo County, New Mexico|Bernalillo County]] District Attorney Sam Bregman to win the Democratic nomination on June 2.<ref name="Haaland">{{cite news |last1=Lee |first1=Morgan |last2=Bryan |first2=Susan Montoya |title=Deb Haaland made history as Interior secretary. Now she's running for governor of New Mexico |url=https://apnews.com/article/deb-haaland-new-mexico-gubernatorial-campaign-284549dfb209b0007d0f9e9e550fb68d |access-date=January 28, 2025 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 28, 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Bregman">{{cite news |last1=Rodriguez |first1=Vince |title=Sam Bregman announces candidacy for Governor in 2026 election |url=https://www.koat.com/article/sam-bregman-governor-candidate-2026-election/64435375 |access-date=April 10, 2025 |work=[[KOAT-TV]] |date=April 10, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> 

[[Rio Rancho, New Mexico|Rio Rancho]] mayor [[Gregg Hull]]<ref name="HullNM">{{cite news |last1=Hendircks |first1=Kevin |title=Rio Rancho mayor will join race for GOP nomination for governor |url=https://nmpoliticalreport.com/2025/04/15/rio-rancho-mayor-will-join-race-for-gop-nomination-for-governor/ |access-date=April 15, 2025 |work=[[New Mexico Political Report]] |date=April 15, 2025}}</ref> won the Republican nomination defeating former secretary of the New Mexico Human Services Department Duke Rodriguez<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowling |first=Joshua |date=2025-12-15 |title=Duke Rodriguez formally announces Republican bid for governor • Source New Mexico |url=https://sourcenm.com/2025/12/15/duke-rodriguez-formally-announces-republican-bid-for-governor/ |access-date=2026-03-22 |website=Source New Mexico |language=en-US}}</ref> and businessman Doug Turner.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Prokop |first=Danielle |date=2026-01-23 |title=New Mexico Election 2026: trail notes • Source New Mexico |url=https://sourcenm.com/2026/01/23/new-mexico-election-2026-trail-notes-3/ |access-date=2026-03-22 |website=Source New Mexico |language=en-US}}</ref>

{{Main|2026 New York gubernatorial election}}

Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Kathy Hochul]] is running for re-election to a second full term.<ref name="HochulRunning">{{Cite web |last=Parsnow |first=Luke |date=July 2, 2024 |title=Hochul says she's running for another term as New York governor in 2026 |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/central-ny/politics/2024/07/02/hochul-says-she-s-running-for-another-term-as-governor-in-2026 |access-date=August 20, 2024 |website=[[Spectrum News]] |language=en |archive-date=July 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240708215410/https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/central-ny/politics/2024/07/02/hochul-says-she-s-running-for-another-term-as-governor-in-2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Primary elections]] took place on June 23, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=May 9, 2025|title=2026 State Primary Election Dates|url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260423040741/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-date=April 23, 2026|access-date=August 5, 2025|website=[[National Conference of State Legislatures|NCSL]]}}</ref> The gubernatorial candidates selected their running mates, instead of having separate primaries.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cuza|first=Bobby|date=May 8, 2025|title=State lawmakers eliminate lieutenant governor primary|url=https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/politics/2025/05/09/albany-lawmakers-eliminate-lieutenant-governor-primary?cid=share_clip|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260105102847/https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/politics/2025/05/09/albany-lawmakers-eliminate-lieutenant-governor-primary?cid=share_clip|archive-date=January 5, 2026|website=[[Spectrum News]]}}</ref> 

Hochul will face Nassau County executive [[Bruce Blakeman]], the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee, in the general election. After U.S. representative [[Elise Stefanik]] withdrew from the Republican primary in December 2025, Blakeman was endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]].<ref name="te">{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/12/20/trump-new-york-governor-endorsement-bruce-blakeman-00702013|title=Trump endorses in New York governor race the day after Stefanik drops out|date=December 20, 2025|website=POLITICO}}</ref> Republicans have not won a statewide election in New York since [[George Pataki]] was re-elected governor in [[2002 New York gubernatorial election|2002]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://abc7ny.com/post/new-york-rep-elise-stefanik-announce-run-governor-soon-friday/18122558/|title=Rep. Elise Stefanik to announce run for New York governor as soon as Friday|date=November 6, 2025|website=ABC7 New York}}</ref>

{{Main|2026 Ohio gubernatorial election}}

Governor [[Mike DeWine]], a Republican, was re-elected in [[2022 Ohio gubernatorial election|2022]] with 62.4% of the vote. He will be term-limited by the [[Constitution of Ohio|Ohio Constitution]] in 2026 and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term. 

On the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] side, [[Biotechnology|biotech]] entrepreneur and former candidate for the [[2024 Republican Party presidential primaries|Republican Party nomination]] in the 2024 presidential election [[Vivek Ramaswamy]] has announced a campaign, which has won the support of President Trump and Vice President Vance, the latter an Ohioan.<ref name="Ramaswamy">{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2025 |title=Millionaire Vivek Ramaswamy set to join the Ohio governor's race |url=https://apnews.com/article/election-2026-ohio-governor-vivek-ramaswamy-799f0c8bdb38c43cd1c2846411867711 |access-date=February 24, 2025 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Henninger |first=Taylor |date=2025-10-16 |title=Vivek Ramaswamy to make campaign stop in Ashland on Friday |url=https://www.ashlandsource.com/2025/10/16/vivek-ramaswamy-to-make-campaign-stop-in-ashland-on-friday/ |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=Ashland Source - Ashland County Ohio News & Info |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Ohio Attorney General|Ohio attorney general]] [[Dave Yost]], who announced his candidacy for governor in January 2025, withdrew from the race and endorsed Ramaswamy in May 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jordan |first1=Felicia |title='I am simply not that important' {{!}} AG Dave Yost suspends his campaign to be Ohio's governor |url=https://www.wcpo.com/news/state/state-ohio/ag-dave-yost-suspends-his-campaign-to-be-ohios-governor |access-date=May 16, 2025 |work=[[WCPO-TV]] |date=May 16, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Ramaswamy defeated automotive entrepreneur Casey Putsch in the Republican primary on May 5, 2026.

Former [[Ohio Department of Health]] Director [[Amy Acton|Dr. Amy Acton]] is the Democratic nominee, as no other candidate filed by the February 4, 2026 deadline.<ref name="ActonOH">{{Cite web|url=https://www.axios.com/local/columbus/2025/01/07/amy-acton-ohio-governor-run-campaign|title=Amy Acton, former state health director, to campaign for Ohio governor|first=Tyler|last=Buchanan|date=January 7, 2025|website=Axios}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Press Releases - Ohio Secretary of State |url=https://www.ohiosos.gov/office/media-center/categories/press-releases |access-date=2026-03-22 |website=www.ohiosos.gov |language=en}}</ref>

[[Governor of Oklahoma|Governor]] [[Kevin Stitt]], a Republican, was re-elected in [[2022 Oklahoma gubernatorial election|2022]] with 55.4% of the vote. He will be term-limited by the [[Constitution of Oklahoma|Oklahoma Constitution]] in 2026 and cannot seek re-election to a third term. 

[[Oklahoma Attorney General|Attorney General]] [[Gentner Drummond]],<ref name="DrummondOK">{{cite news |last1=Evans |first1=Murray |title=AG Gentner Drummond announces bid for Oklahoma governor in 2026 election |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/politics/state/2025/01/13/oklahoma-elections-gentner-drummond-campaign-governor-2026/77603880007/ |access-date=January 13, 2025 |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |date=January 13, 2025}}</ref> former Oklahoma Secretary of Budget [[Mike Mazzei]],<ref name="Mazzei">{{cite news |last1=Media |first1=Griffin |title=Oklahoma Governor race: Former State Sen. Mike Mazzei announces candidacy |url=https://www.newson6.com/story/67ea7ca61e03566cb076c088/oklahoma-governor-race-mike-mazzei |access-date=March 31, 2025 |work=[[KOTV-DT]] |date=March 31, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> former Speaker of the [[Oklahoma House of Representatives]] [[Charles McCall]],<ref name="McCall">{{cite news |last1=Media |first1=Griffin |title=Oklahoma Governor race: Charles McCall files for candidacy |url=https://www.news9.com/story/67b48d06a128e54ee89ada96/oklahoma-governor-race-charles-mccall-files-for-candidacy |access-date=February 18, 2025 |work=[[KWTV-DT]] |date=February 18, 2025 |language=en}}</ref>  former [[Oklahoma Secretary of Public Safety]] [[Chip Keating]],<ref name="Keating">{{cite web |last1=Metzer |first1=Steve |title=Chip Keating announces run for governor |url=https://tulsaworld.com/news/state-regional/government-politics/article_f51a889e-1eec-4ddb-bd98-f52845f8c50b.html |access-date=October 2, 2025 |work=[[Tulsa World]] |date=October 1, 2025}}</ref> who is the son of former governor [[Frank Keating]], and former [[Oklahoma Senate|state senator]] [[Jake A. Merrick]]<ref name="Merrick">{{cite news |last1=Ramos |first1=Lionel |title=Former lawmaker Jake Merrick joins race for Oklahoma Governor |url=https://www.kosu.org/politics/2025-05-01/former-lawmaker-jake-merrick-joins-race-for-oklahoma-governor |access-date=May 1, 2025 |work=[[KOSU]] |date=May 1, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> all ran for the Republican nomination. Drummond and Mazzei advanced to a runoff, which took place on August 25. Mazzei narrowly defeated Drummond with 50.3% of the vote to become the Republican nominee. 

[[Oklahoma House of Representatives|State representative]] [[Cyndi Munson]]<ref name="MunsonOK">{{cite news |last1=Media |first1=Griffin |title=Oklahoma House Rep. Cyndi Munson announces run for governor |url=https://www.newson6.com/story/67fe3542ef0ad866d416aaad/oklahoma-house-rep-cyndi-munson-announces-run-for-governor |access-date=April 15, 2025 |work=[[KOTV-DT]] |date=April 15, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> defeated securities trader Arya Azma<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hickey |first=Olivia |date=2025-11-24 |title=Gov. Kevin Stitt weighs in on crowded gubernatorial race, says he won't back AG Drummond |url=https://www.koco.com/article/kevin-stitt-governors-gubernatorial-race-ag-gentner-drummond/69533056 |access-date=2026-03-25 |website=KOCO |language=en}}</ref> for the Democratic nomination.
