{{See also|2026 Rhode Island lieutenant gubernatorial election}}
Governor [[Dan McKee]], a Democrat, took office in 2021 following the resignation of [[Gina Raimondo]] and was elected to a full term in [[2022 Rhode Island gubernatorial election|2022]] with 57.9% of the vote.<ref name=DanMcKee>{{cite news |last1=Fortier |first1=Marc |title=RI Gov. Dan McKee announces reelection campaign |url=https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/ri-gov-dan-mckee-announces-reelection-campaign/3646001/ |access-date=March 3, 2025 |work=[[NBC10 Boston]] |date=March 3, 2025}}</ref>

[[Helena Foulkes]], a former [[CVS Pharmacy]] executive, challenged McKee in a rematch of their closely contested 2022 primary.<ref name="Foulkes">{{cite web |last=Anderson |first=Patrick |date=September 9, 2025 |title=Helena Foulkes launches second bid for governor. What we know. |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/news/politics/2025/09/09/helena-foulkes-launches-bid-to-unseat-mckee-as-ri-governor-in-2026/86055267007/ |access-date=September 9, 2025 |publisher=[[The Providence Journal]] |lang=en}}</ref> Foulkes won the nomination, defeating McKee and making him the first elected governor to lose renomination since [[2014 Hawaii gubernatorial election|2014]].{{efn|Governor [[Jeff Colyer]] of Kansas, who had taken office after the resignation of [[Sam Brownback]], was defeated by [[Kris Kobach]] in the [[2018 Kansas gubernatorial election|2018]] primary election.}}

2022 lieutenant governor nominee [[Aaron Guckian]]<ref name="Guckian">{{cite web |last1=Fitzpatrick |first1=Edward |title=Republican Aaron Guckian to run for governor of Rhode Island |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/11/30/metro/ri-republican-aaron-guckian-governor/ |access-date=November 30, 2025 |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |date=November 30, 2025}}</ref> defeated actress Elaine Pelino for the Republican nomination.<ref name="Pelino">{{cite web |last1=Gregg |first1=Katherine |title=These are the wild-card GOP candidates who are running or might run for RI top offices |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/news/politics/2025/11/03/ri-republican-candidate-field-in-2026-begins-to-take-shape/86609140007/ |access-date=November 14, 2025 |work=[[Providence Journal]] |date=November 3, 2025 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Pelino subsequently requested a recount, which was approved by the Rhode Island Board of Elections. The recount did not change the outcome.<ref>{{Cite web |last=NEWS |first=NBC 10 |date=2026-09-15 |title=Recount does not change outcome of Republican primary in governor's race |url=https://turnto10.com/news/local/officials-begin-recount-of-republican-primary-for-rhode-island-governor-sept-15-2026 |access-date=2026-09-15 |website=WJAR |language=en}}</ref>

[[Governor of South Dakota|Governor]] [[Larry Rhoden]], a Republican, assumed office in 2025 following the resignation of [[Kristi Noem]] to become [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|Secretary of Homeland Security]].<ref name="Rhoden">{{cite news |author=C.J. Keene |title=Gov. Larry Rhoden officially announces reelection campaign |url=https://www.sdpb.org/politics/2025-11-18/gov-larry-rhoden-officially-announces-reelection-campaign |access-date=November 18, 2025 |work=[[SDPB]] |date=November 18, 2025}}</ref> Noem had been re-elected in [[2022 South Dakota gubernatorial election|2022]] with 62% of the vote. Rhoden is now running for a full term.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keene |first=C. J. |date=2025-11-18 |title=Gov. Larry Rhoden officially announces election campaign |url=https://www.sdpb.org/politics/2025-11-18/gov-larry-rhoden-officially-announces-election-campaign |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=SDPB |language=en}}</ref>

Challenging Rhoden in the Republican primary were Speaker of the [[South Dakota House of Representatives]] [[Jon Hansen]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Huber |first=Makenzie |date=2025-04-25 |title=First candidate for governor focuses on property rights, spending and halting 'corporate welfare' • South Dakota Searchlight |url=https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2025/04/24/first-candidate-governor-race-jon-hansen-focuses-property-rights-spending-cuts-halting-corporate-welfare-karla-lems/ |access-date=2026-03-29 |website=South Dakota Searchlight |language=en-US}}</ref> U.S. Representative [[Dusty Johnson]]<ref name="dustyjohnson">{{cite news |title=Saying it's time for a 'new chapter,' Dusty Johnson announces his campaign for governor • South Dakota Searchlight |url=https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2025/06/30/dusty-johnson-makes-it-official-with-announcement-of-campaign-for-governor/ |access-date=June 30, 2025 |work=South Dakota Searchlight |date=June 30, 2025}}</ref> and real estate entrepreneur Toby Doeden.<ref name="Doerden">{{cite news |last1=Sneve |first1=Joe |title=Toby Doeden will run in South Dakota's next election for governor |url=https://www.thedakotascout.com/p/toby-doeden-will-run-in-south-dakotas |access-date=May 23, 2025 |work=The Dakota Scout |date=May 23, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Doeden and Rhoden advanced to a runoff, which took place on July 28. Rhoden defeated Doeden in a landslide in the runoff and became the nominee.

On the Democratic side, [[South Dakota Democratic Party]] executive director [[Daniel Ahlers]]<ref name="Ahlers">{{cite news |title=Leader of South Dakota Democratic Party announces his campaign for governor |url=https://southdakotasearchlight.com/briefs/leader-of-south-dakota-democratic-party-announces-his-campaign-for-governor/ |access-date=February 9, 2026 |work=South Dakota Searchlight |date=February 9, 2026}}</ref> is the nominee.

U.S. Senator [[Marsha Blackburn]],<ref name="BlackburnTN">{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Sarah Grace |title=Marsha Blackburn announces run for Governor of Tennessee |url=https://nashvillebanner.com/2025/08/06/marsha-blackburn-tennessee-governor-campaign-launch/ |access-date=August 6, 2025 |work=Nashville Banner |date=August 6, 2025}}</ref> state representative [[Monty Fritts]],<ref name="FrittsTN">{{cite news |last1=Grace Taylor |first1=Sarah |title=State Rep. Governor [[Greg Abbott]], a Republican, was re-elected in [[2022 Texas gubernatorial election|2022]] with 54.8% of the vote. Because [[Texas]] does not have gubernatorial term limits in its [[Constitution of Texas|Constitution]], he is eligible to run for re-election to a fourth term. On March 1, 2024, Abbott announced his intention to seek re-election.<ref name=absolutely>{{cite web |url= https://www.texastribune.org/2025/11/09/texas-greg-abbott-reelection-campaign-governor/ |title=Gov. Greg Abbott launches reelection campaign for fourth term |date=November 9, 2025 |access-date=November 9, 2025 |publisher=[[The Texas Tribune]] |last=Gou |first=Kayla}}</ref> He won the primary with over 80% of the vote.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McGaughy |first1=Lauren |title=Greg Abbott's Primary Win Sets the Stage for a Record Fourth Term as Texas Governor |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/04/us/elections/abbott-texas-politics.html |access-date=4 March 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 4, 2026}}</ref> 

The Democratic nominee is state representative [[Gina Hinojosa]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wermund |first1=Benjamin |title=Greg Abbott to face Democrat Gina Hinojosa in bid for a record fourth term as Texas governor |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/politics/election/2026/article/governor-primary-results-21329304.php |access-date=4 March 2026 |work=Houston Chronicle |date=March 3, 2026}}</ref> Hinojosa beat [[Chris Bell (politician)|Chris Bell]], a former U.S. representative for [[Texas's 25th congressional district]] and former candidate for governor in [[2006 Texas gubernatorial election|2006]], [[mayor of Houston]] in [[2001 Houston mayoral election|2001]] and [[2015 Houston mayoral election|2015]], and U.S. Senate in [[2020 United States Senate election in Texas|2020]], and Bobby Cole, a rancher, in the primary.<ref name="BellTX">{{Cite news |title=Another candidate joins race for Texas governor |url=https://www.kvue.com/video/news/politics/vote-texas/race-texas-governor-chris-bell/269-d5eefaba-5a93-4566-9d9c-ddb9b3fa93c3 |date=November 10, 2025 |access-date=November 11, 2025 |work=KVUE}}</ref><ref name="HinojosaTX">{{cite web |last1=McKim |first1=Dylan |title=State Rep. Gina Hinojosa enters race for Texas governor |url=https://www.kxan.com/news/texas-politics/state-rep-gina-hinojosa-enters-race-for-texas-governor/ |access-date=October 15, 2025 |work=[[KXAN Austin]] |date=October 15, 2025}}</ref><ref name="ColeTX">{{Cite news |last=Bugenhagen |first=Faith |title=Can an East Texas farmer upset Greg Abbott for governor? |url=https://www.chron.com//politics/article/texas-governor-election-2026-20392211.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250627100559/https://www.chron.com//politics/article/texas-governor-election-2026-20392211.php |archive-date=June 27, 2025 |access-date=July 23, 2025 |work=Chron |language=en}}</ref>

{{Main|2026 Vermont gubernatorial election}}

{{See also|2026 Vermont lieutenant gubernatorial election}}

Governor [[Phil Scott]], a Republican, was re-elected in [[2024 Vermont gubernatorial election|2024]] with 73.4% of the vote. Scott is running for a sixth two-year term, declaring only hours before the filing deadline was required. He won the primary unopposed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=Shaun Robinson, Charlotte |date=2026-05-28 |title=Gov. Phil Scott is running for reelection |url=https://vtdigger.org/2026/05/28/gov-phil-scott-is-running-for-reelection/ |access-date=2026-05-28 |website=VTDigger |language=en-US}}</ref> 

For the Democrats, economist Amanda Janoo is the nominee.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McCallum |first1=Kevin |title=Amanda Janoo Announces Bid for Vermont Governor |url=https://www.sevendaysvt.com/news/amanda-janoo-announces-bid-for-vermont-governor/ |access-date=March 10, 2026 |work=[[Seven Days (newspaper)|Seven Days]] |date=March 10, 2026}}</ref> She narrowly defeated former lobbying group CEO Aly Richards in the primary. [[Vermont Attorney General|Attorney General]] [[Charity Clark]] was considered a potential candidate and had previously said she that she would run for statewide office in 2026, but she instead decided to seek re-election to her current office.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Shaun |date=2025-08-14 |title=Vermont Lt. Gov. John Rodgers, Secretary of State Sarah Copeland Hanzas say they're running for reelection |url=https://vtdigger.org/2025/08/14/vermont-lt-gov-john-rodgers-secretary-of-state-sarah-copeland-hanzas-say-theyre-running-for-reelection/ |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=[[VTDigger]]|language=en-US}}</ref> [[Vermont State Treasurer|State Treasurer]] [[Mike Pieciak]] was reported to have considered a campaign for the governor, but he too choose to seek re-election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Shaun |date=2025-10-14 |title=Vermont Treasurer Mike Pieciak hires top staffer from Rep. Becca Balint |url=https://vtdigger.org/2025/10/14/vermont-treasurer-mike-pieciak-hires-top-staffer-from-rep-becca-balint/ |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=[[VTDigger]]|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=Charlotte |date=2026-05-28 |title=Mike Pieciak runs again for treasurer — not governor |url=https://vtdigger.org/2026/05/28/mike-pieciak-runs-again-for-treasurer-not-governor/ |access-date=2026-05-28 |website=VTDigger |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[Dean Roy]], a 14-year-old from [[Stowe, Vermont|Stowe]], is running as a member of the Freedom and Unity Party.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 20, 2025 |title=Stowe teen preps for gubernatorial race |url=https://vtdigger.org/2025/07/20/stowe-teen-preps-for-gubernatorial-race/ |access-date=July 27, 2025 |website=[[VTDigger]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Vermont has no minimum age requirement for the governorship, allowing Roy to seek the governorship despite not being old enough to vote.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-08-13 |title=14-year-old boy uses legal quirk to run for Vermont governor |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/14-year-old-boy-uses-legal-quirk-run-vermont-governor-n900261 |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=[[NBC News]] |language=en}}</ref>

{{Main|2026 Wisconsin gubernatorial election}}

Governor [[Tony Evers]], a Democrat, was re-elected in [[2022 Wisconsin gubernatorial election|2022]] with 51.2% of the vote. Despite [[Wisconsin]] not having gubernatorial term limits in its [[Constitution of Wisconsin|Constitution]], Evers announced on July 24, 2025, that he would not seek re-election.<ref name="Evers">{{cite news |title=Tony Evers will not seek a third term as governor of Wisconsin |url=https://www.tmj4.com/news/state-capitol/tony-evers-will-not-seek-a-third-term-as-governor-of-wisconsin |access-date=July 24, 2025 |work=[[WTMJ-TV]] |date=July 24, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> 

Former [[Lieutenant Governor of Wisconsin|Lieutenant Governor]] and in [[2022 United States Senate election in Wisconsin|2022]] nominee for U.S. Senate [[Mandela Barnes]],<ref name="MandelaWI">{{cite web |last2=Glueck |first2=Katie |last1=Epstein |first1=Reid J. |title=Mandela Barnes Enters Wisconsin Governor Race, Joining Crowded Field of Democrats |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/02/us/politics/wisconsin-governor-mandela-barnes.html |access-date=December 2, 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=December 2, 2025}}</ref> state senator [[Kelda Roys]],<ref name="RoysWI">{{cite news |last1=Schmidt |first1=Mitchell |title=Madison Democratic Sen. Kelda Roys launches bid for governor |url=https://madison.com/news/state-regional/government-politics/elections/article_21376a23-88fe-4ee0-ac90-768852f84bd4.html |access-date=September 15, 2025 |work=Wisconsin State Journal |date=September 15, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> state representative [[Francesca Hong]],<ref name="Hong">{{cite news |first1=Anya |last1=van Wagtendonk |work=[[Wisconsin Public Radio]] |access-date=September 17, 2025 |url=https://www.wpr.org/news/madison-francesca-hong-democrat-governor-campaign-2026 |date=September 17, 2025 |title=Madison Rep. Francesca Hong joins Democratic primary for governor}}</ref> and Milwaukee County executive [[David Crowley (Wisconsin politician)|David Crowley]]<ref name="Crowley">{{cite web |last1=Svirnovskiy |first1=Gregory |title=David Crowley reenters Wisconsin governor's race with Evers endorsement |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/18/david-crowley-reenters-wisconsin-governors-race-with-evers-endorsement-01004326 |access-date=July 19, 2025 |work=[[Politico]] |date=July 18, 2026}}</ref> have all announced campaigns for the Democratic nomination.

U.S. Representative for [[Wisconsin's 7th congressional district]] [[Tom Tiffany]] and medical service technician Andy Manske<ref>{{Cite web |last=McGroarty |first=Erin |date=2025-10-07 |title=Wisconsin governor candidates: How can any of 11 stand out? |url=https://captimes.com/news/elections/wisconsin-governor-candidates-how-can-any-of-11-stand-out/article_aa319ff2-97fd-49d9-9c16-5f4cdf9b4918.html |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=The Cap Times |language=en}}</ref> have both announced campaigns for the Republican nomination.<ref name="Tiffany">{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Matt |date=September 23, 2025 |access-date=September 23, 2025 |work=[[WISN-TV|WISN]] |url=https://www.wisn.com/article/gop-rep-tom-tiffany-launches-campaign-for-governor/68022421 |title=GOP Rep. Tom Tiffany launches campaign for governor}}</ref>

Governor [[Mark Gordon]], a Republican, was re-elected in [[2022 Wyoming gubernatorial election|2022]] with 74.1% of the vote. He will be term-limited by state law in 2026 and cannot seek reelection to a third consecutive term.

State senator [[Eric Barlow]]<ref name="Barlow">{{cite news |last1=Hill |first1=Alex |title=Wyoming Senator Eric Barlow announces 2026 gubernatorial campaign |url=https://www.yourwyominglink.com/news/politics/wyoming-senator-eric-barlow-announces-2026-gubernatorial-campaign/article_932d7583-9c74-4bc4-80fb-5fde1c577234.html |access-date=August 13, 2025 |work=Your Wyoming Link |date=August 13, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> defeated [[Wyoming Department of Education|Wyoming Superintendent of Public Instruction]] [[Megan Degenfelder]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eagle |first=Noah Zahn Wyoming Tribune |date=2026-01-12 |title=Degenfelder announces bid for governor after Trump endorsement |url=https://www.wyomingnews.com/news/local_news/degenfelder-announces-bid-for-governor-after-trump-endorsement/article_f5ec3cdb-7271-4c54-b1b1-a9ee8e6b17fd.html |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=Wyoming Tribune Eagle |language=en}}</ref> and civil engineer Brent Bien<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |url=https://cowboystatedaily.com/2024/11/16/republican-brent-bien-first-to-announce-campaign-for-wyoming-governor-in-2026/ |title=Republican Brent Bien First to Announce Campaign for Wyoming Governor in 2026 |access-date=November 26, 2024 |archive-date=November 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241117131502/https://cowboystatedaily.com/2024/11/16/republican-brent-bien-first-to-announce-campaign-for-wyoming-governor-in-2026/ |url-status=live }}</ref> for the Republican nomination. 

Perennial candidate Kenneth Casner is the Democratic nominee.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Wyoming Secretary of State |author1-link=Secretary of State of Wyoming |title=2026 Primary Election Candidate Roster |url=https://sos.wyo.gov/Elections/Docs/2026/2026_WY_Primary_Election_Candidates.pdf |access-date=16 June 2026 |date=15 June 2026}}</ref>
